title: Winner's Curse Drives False Promises in Data-Driven Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2602.08892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: A major challenge in data-driven decision-making is accurate policy evaluation---i.e., guaranteeing that a learned decision-making policy achieves the promised benefits. A popular strategy is model-based policy evaluation, which estimates a model from data to infer counterfactual outcomes. This strategy is known to produce unwarrantedly optimistic estimates of the true benefit due to the winner's curse. We searched the recent literature on data-driven decision-making, identifying a sample of 55 papers published in Management Science in the past decade; all but two relied on this flawed methodology. Several common justifications are provided: (1) the estimated models are accurate, stable, and well-calibrated, (2) the historical data uses random treatment assignment, (3) the model family is well-specified, and (4) the evaluation methodology uses sample splitting. Unfortunately, we show that no combination of these justifications

translated_title: 赢者诅咒导致数据驱动决策中的虚假承诺
translated_abstract: 数据驱动决策中的一项重大挑战是准确的政策评估——即保证学习到的决策策略能够实现所承诺的收益。一种流行的策略是基于模型的政策评估，即从数据中估计一个模型来推断反事实结果。众所周知，由于赢者诅咒（winner's curse），这种策略会产生对真实收益的过度乐观估计。我们搜索了近期关于数据驱动决策的文献，识别出过去十年发表在《管理科学》（Management Science）上的55篇论文样本；其中除两篇外，其余全部依赖于这种有缺陷的方法。文献中通常给出以下几种辩护理由：(1) 估计出的模型准确、稳定且校准良好；(2) 历史数据采用随机处理分配；(3) 模型族设定正确；(4) 评估方法使用样本分割。遗憾的是，我们证明这些辩护理由的任何组合都无法消除这一问题。
tldr: 本文通过对近十年《管理科学》55篇论文的实证审查与理论分析，揭示了基于模型的政策评估因赢者诅咒而系统性高估决策收益，且模型精度、随机处理分配、正确模型设定和样本分割等常见辩护理由均无法消除这一乐观偏差。
